{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T190912Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/.claude/skills/frontend-playbook\n\n# Frontend Playbook\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**\"I'll use `yarn chain`.\"** Wrong. `yarn chain` gives you an empty local chain with no protocols, no tokens, no state. `yarn fork --network base` gives you a copy of real Base with Uniswap, Aave, USDC, real whale balances — everything (verified addresses: `addresses/SKILL.md`). Always fork.\n\n**\"I deployed to IPFS and it works.\"** Did the CID change? If not, you deployed stale output. Did routes work? Without `trailingSlash: true`, every route except `/` returns 404. Did you check the OG image? Without `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL`, it points to `localhost:3000`.\n\n**\"I'll set up the project manually.\"** Don't. `npx create-eth@latest` handles everything — Foundry, Next.js, RainbowKit, scaffold hooks. Never run `forge init` or create Next.js projects from scratch.\n\n---\n\n## Fork Mode Setup\n\n### Why Fork, Not Chain\n\n```\nyarn chain (WRONG)              yarn fork --network base (CORRECT)\n└─ Empty local chain            └─ Fork of real Base mainnet\n└─ No protocols                 └─ Uniswap, Aave, etc. available\n└─ No tokens                    └─ Real USDC, WETH exist\n└─ Testing in isolation         └─ Test against REAL state\n```\n\n### Setup\n\n```bash\nnpx create-eth@latest          # Select: foundry, target chain, name\ncd <project-name>\nyarn install\nyarn fork --network base       # Terminal 1: fork of real Base\nyarn deploy                    # Terminal 2: deploy contracts to fork\nyarn start                     # Terminal 3: Next.js frontend\n```\n\n### Critical: Chain ID Gotcha\n\n**When using fork mode, the frontend target network MUST be `chains.foundry` (chain ID 31337), NOT the chain you're forking.**\n\nThe fork runs locally on Anvil with chain ID 31337. Even if you're forking Base:\n\n```typescript\n// scaffold.config.ts during development\ntargetNetworks: [chains.foundry],  // ✅ NOT chains.base!\n```\n\nOnly switch to `chains.base` when deploying contracts to the REAL network.\n\n### Enable Block Mining\n\n```bash\n# In a new terminal — REQUIRED for time-dependent logic\ncast rpc anvil_setIntervalMining 1\n```\n\nWithout this, `block.timestamp` stays FROZEN. Any contract logic using timestamps (deadlines, expiry, vesting) will break silently.\n\n**Make it permanent** by editing `packages/foundry/package.json` to add `--block-time 1` to the fork script.\n\n---\n\n## Deploying to IPFS (Recommended)\n\nIPFS is the recommended deploy path for SE2. Avoids Vercel's memory limits entirely. Produces a fully decentralized static site.\n\n### Full Build Command\n\n```bash\ncd packages/nextjs\nrm -rf .next out  # ALWAYS clean first\n\nNEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://yourapp.yourname.eth.link\" \\\n  NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IGNORE_BUILD_ERROR=true \\\n  yarn build\n\n# Upload to BuidlGuidl IPFS\nyarn bgipfs upload out\n# Save the CID!\n```\n\n### Node 25+ localStorage Polyfill (REQUIRED)\n\nNode.js 25+ ships a built-in `localStorage` object that's MISSING standard WebStorage API methods (`getItem`, `setItem`). This breaks `next-themes`, RainbowKit, and any library that calls `localStorage.getItem()` during static page generation.\n\n**Error you'll see:**\n```\nTypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function\nError occurred prerendering page \"/_not-found\"\n```\n\n**The fix:** Create `polyfill-localstorage.cjs` in `packages/nextjs/`:\n```javascript\nif (typeof globalThis.localStorage !== \"undefined\" &&\n    typeof globalThis.localStorage.getItem !== \"function\") {\n  const store = new Map();\n  globalThis.localStorage = {\n    getItem: (key) => store.get(key) ?? null,\n    setItem: (key, value) => store.set(key, String(value)),\n    removeItem: (key) => store.delete(key),\n    clear: () => store.clear(),\n    key: (index) => [...store.keys()][index] ?? null,\n    get length() { return store.size; },\n  };\n}\n```\n\n**Why `--require` and not `instrumentation.ts`?** Next.js spawns a separate build worker process for prerendering. `--require` injects into EVERY Node process (including workers). `next.config.ts` polyfill only runs in the main process. `instrumentation.ts` doesn't run in the build worker. Only `--require` works.\n\n### IPFS Routing — Why Routes Break\n\nIPFS gateways serve static files. No server handles routing. Three things MUST be true:\n\n**1. `output: \"export\"` in next.config.ts** — generates static HTML files.\n\n**2. `trailingSlash: true` (CRITICAL)** — This is the #1 reason routes break:\n- `trailingSlash: false` (default) → generates `debug.html`\n- `trailingSlash: true` → generates `debug/index.html`\n- IPFS gateways resolve directories to `index.html` automatically, but NOT bare filenames\n- Without trailing slash: `/debug` → 404 ❌\n- With trailing slash: `/debug` → `debug/` → `debug/index.html` ✅\n\n**3. Pages must survive static prerendering** — any page that crashes during `yarn build` (browser APIs at import time, localStorage) gets skipped silently → 404 on IPFS.\n\n**The complete IPFS-safe next.config.ts pattern:**\n```typescript\nconst isIpfs = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD === \"true\";\nif (isIpfs) {\n  nextConfig.output = \"export\";\n  nextConfig.trailingSlash = true;\n  nextConfig.images = { unoptimized: true };\n}\n```\n\n**SE2's block explorer pages** use `localStorage` at import time and crash during static export. Rename `app/blockexplorer` to `app/_blockexplorer-disabled` if not needed.\n\n### Stale Build Detection\n\n**The #1 IPFS footgun:** You edit code, then deploy the OLD build.\n\n```bash\n# MANDATORY after ANY code change:\nrm -rf .next out                     # 1. Delete old artifacts\n# ... run full build command ...     # 2. Rebuild from scratch\ngrep -l \"YOUR_STRING\" out/_next/static/chunks/app/*.js  # 3. Verify changes present\n\n# Timestamp check:\nstat -f '%Sm' app/page.tsx           # Source modified time\nstat -f '%Sm' out/                   # Build output time\n# Source NEWER than out/ = STALE BUILD. Rebuild first!\n```\n\n**The CID is proof:** If the IPFS CID didn't change after a deploy, you deployed the same content. A real code change ALWAYS produces a new CID.\n\n### Verify Routes After Deploy\n\n```bash\nls out/*/index.html                  # Each route has a directory + index.html\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\" -L \"https://GATEWAY/ipfs/CID/debug/\"\n# Should return 200, not 404\n```\n\n---\n\n## Deploying to Vercel (Alternative)\n\nSE2 is a monorepo — Vercel needs special configuration.\n\n### Configuration\n\n1. **Root Directory:** `packages/nextjs`\n2. **Install Command:** `cd ../.. && yarn install`\n3. **Build Command:** leave default (`next build`)\n4. **Output Directory:** leave default (`.next`)\n\n```bash\n# Via API:\ncurl -X PATCH \"https://api.vercel.com/v9/projects/PROJECT_ID\" \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $VERCEL_TOKEN\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\"rootDirectory\": \"packages/nextjs\", \"installCommand\": \"cd ../.. && yarn install\"}'\n```\n\n### Common Failures\n\n| Error | Cause | Fix |\n|-------|-------|-----|\n| \"No Next.js version detected\" | Root Directory not set | Set to `packages/nextjs` |\n| \"cd packages/nextjs: No such file\" | Build command has `cd` | Clear it — root dir handles this |\n| OOM / exit code 129 | SE2 monorepo exceeds 8GB | Use IPFS instead, or `vercel --prebuilt` |\n\n### Decision Tree\n\n```\nWant to deploy SE2?\n├─ IPFS (recommended) → yarn ipfs / manual build + upload\n│   └─ Fully decentralized, no memory limits, works with ENS\n├─ Vercel → Set rootDirectory + installCommand\n│   └─ Fast CDN, but centralized. May OOM on large projects\n└─ vercel --prebuilt → Build locally, push artifacts to Vercel\n    └─ Best of both: local build power + Vercel CDN\n```\n\n---\n\n## ENS Subdomain Setup\n\nTwo mainnet transactions to point an ENS subdomain at your IPFS deployment.\n\n### Transaction 1: Create Subdomain (new apps only)\n\n1. Open `https://app.ens.domains/yourname.eth`\n2. Go to \"Subnames\" tab → \"New subname\"\n3. Enter the label (e.g. `myapp`) → Next → Skip profile → Open Wallet → Confirm\n4. If gas is stuck: switch MetaMask to Ethereum → Activity tab → \"Speed up\"\n\n### Transaction 2: Set IPFS Content Hash\n\n1. Navigate to `https://app.ens.domains/myapp.yourname.eth`\n2. \"Records\" tab → \"Edit Records\" → \"Other\" tab\n3. Paste in Content Hash field: `ipfs://<CID>`\n4. Save → Open Wallet → Confirm in MetaMask\n\nFor **updates** to an existing app: skip Tx 1, only do Tx 2.\n\n### Verify\n\n```bash\n# 1. Onchain content hash matches\nRESOLVER=$(cast call 0x00000000000C2e074eC69A0dFb2997BA6C7d2e1e \\\n  \"resolver(bytes32)(address)\" $(cast namehash myapp.yourname.eth) \\\n  --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com)\ncast call $RESOLVER \"contenthash(bytes32)(bytes)\" \\\n  $(cast namehash myapp.yourname.eth) --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com\n\n# 2. Gateway responds (may take 5-15 min for cache)\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\" -L \"https://myapp.yourname.eth.link\"\n\n# 3. OG metadata correct (not localhost)\ncurl -s -L \"https://myapp.yourname.eth.link\" | grep 'og:image'\n```\n\n**Use `.eth.link` NOT `.eth.limo`** — `.eth.link` works better on mobile.\n\n---\n\n## Go to Production — Complete Checklist\n\nWhen the user says \"ship it\", follow this EXACT sequence.\n\n### Step 1: Final Code Review 🤖\n- All feedback incorporated\n- No duplicate h1, no raw addresses, no shared isLoading\n- `scaffold.config.ts` has `rpcOverrides` and `pollingInterval: 3000`\n\n### Step 2: Choose Domain 👤\nAsk: *\"What subdomain do you want? e.g. `myapp.yourname.eth` → `myapp.yourname.eth.link`\"*\n\n### Step 3: Generate OG Image + Fix Metadata 🤖\n- Create 1200×630 PNG (`public/thumbnail.png`) — NOT the stock SE2 thumbnail\n- Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL` to the live domain\n- Verify `og:image` will resolve to an absolute production URL\n\n### Step 4: Clean Build + IPFS Deploy 🤖\n```bash\ncd packages/nextjs && rm -rf .next out\nNEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://myapp.yourname.eth.link\" \\\n  NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true NEXT_PUBLIC_IGNORE_BUILD_ERROR=true \\\n  yarn build\n\n# Verify before uploading:\nls out/*/index.html                        # Routes exist\ngrep 'og:image' out/index.html             # Not localhost\nstat -f '%Sm' app/page.tsx                 # Source older than out/\nstat -f '%Sm' out/\n\nyarn bgipfs upload out                     # Save the CID\n```\n\n### Step 5: Share for Approval 👤\nSend: *\"Build ready for review: `https://community.bgipfs.com/ipfs/<CID>`\"*\n**Wait for approval before touching ENS.**\n\n### Step 6: Set ENS 🤖\nCreate subdomain (if new) + set IPFS content hash. Two mainnet transactions.\n\n### Step 7: Verify 🤖\n- Content hash matches onchain\n- `.eth.link` gateway responds with 200\n- OG image loads correctly\n- Routes work (`/debug/`, etc.)\n\n### Step 8: Report 👤\n*\"Live at `https://myapp.yourname.eth.link` — ENS content hash confirmed onchain, unfurl metadata set.\"*\n\n---\n\n## Build Verification Process\n\nA build is NOT done when the code compiles. It's done when you've tested it like a real user.\n\n### Phase 1: Code QA (Automated)\n- Scan `.tsx` files for raw address strings (should use `<Address/>`)\n- Scan for shared `isLoading` state across multiple buttons\n- Scan for missing `disabled` props on transaction buttons\n- Verify RPC config and polling interval\n- Verify OG metadata with absolute URLs\n- Verify no public RPCs in any file\n\n### Phase 2: Smart Contract Testing\n```bash\nforge test                    # All tests pass\nforge test --fuzz-runs 10000  # Fuzz testing\n```\nTest edge cases: zero amounts, max amounts, unauthorized callers, reentrancy attempts.\n\n### Phase 3: Browser Testing (THE REAL TEST)\n\nOpen the app and do a FULL walkthrough:\n\n1. **Load the app** — does it render correctly?\n2. **Check page title** — is it correct, not \"Scaffold-ETH 2\"?\n3. **Connect wallet** — does the connect flow work?\n4. **Wrong network** — connect on wrong chain, verify \"Switch to Base\" appears\n5. **Switch network** — click the switch button, verify it works\n6. **Approve flow** — verify approve button shows, click it, wait for tx, verify action button appears\n7. **Main action** — click primary action, verify loader, wait for tx, verify state updates\n8. **Error handling** — reject a transaction in wallet, verify UI recovers\n9. **Address displays** — all addresses showing ENS/blockies, not raw hex?\n10. **Share URL** — check OG unfurl (image, title, description)\n\n### Phase 4: QA Sub-Agent (Complex Builds)\nFor bigger projects, spawn a sub-agent with fresh context. Give it the repo path and deployed URL. It reads all code against the UX rules, opens a browser, clicks through independently, and reports issues.\n\n---\n\n## Don't Do These\n\n- ❌ `yarn chain` — use `yarn fork --network <chain>`\n- ❌ `forge init` — use `npx create-eth@latest`\n- ❌ Manual Next.js setup — SE2 handles it\n- ❌ Manual wallet connection — SE2 has RainbowKit pre-configured\n- ❌ Edit `deployedContracts.ts` — it's auto-generated by `yarn deploy`\n- ❌ Hardcode API keys in `scaffold.config.ts` — use `.env.local`\n- ❌ Use `mainnet.base.org` in production — use Alchemy or similar\n\n---\n\n## Resources\n\n- **SE2 Docs:** https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/\n- **UI Components:** https://ui.scaffoldeth.io/\n- **SpeedRun Ethereum:** https://speedrunethereum.com/\n- **ETH Tech Tree:** https://www.ethtechtree.com\n- **BuidlGuidl IPFS:** https://upload.bgipfs.com\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883f155b-a7ed-4467-8dca-d277ae7a1ce9","uuid":"24417a13-6b26-4ce6-8dde-295a46e8e696","timestamp":"2026-07-24T19:09:21.189Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CekpPUXFqW3QqYdHT2FfHi","type":"tool_result","content":"=== YourContract.sol ===\n//SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity >=0.8.0 <0.9.0;\n\n// Useful for debugging. Remove when deploying to a live network.\nimport \"forge-std/console.sol\";\n\n// Use openzeppelin to inherit battle-tested implementations (ERC20, ERC721, etc)\n// import \"@openzeppelin/contracts/access/Ownable.sol\";\n\n/**\n * A smart contract that allows changing a state variable of the contract and tracking the changes\n * It also allows the owner to withdraw the Ether in the contract\n * @author BuidlGuidl\n */\ncontract YourContract {\n  // State Variables\n  address public immutable owner;\n  string public greeting = \"Building Unstoppable Apps!!!\";\n  bool public premium = false;\n  uint256 public totalCounter = 0;\n  mapping(address => uint256) public userGreetingCounter;\n\n  // Events: a way to emit log statements from smart contract that can be listened to by external parties\n  event GreetingChange(\n    address indexed greetingSetter,\n    string newGreeting,\n    bool premium,\n    uint256 value\n  );\n\n  // Constructor: Called once on contract deployment\n  // Check packages/foundry/deploy/Deploy.s.sol\n  constructor(address _owner) {\n    owner = _owner;\n  }\n\n  // Modifier: used to define a set of rules that must be met before or after a function is executed\n  // Check the withdraw() function\n  modifier isOwner() {\n    // msg.sender: predefined variable that represents address of the account that called the current function\n    require(msg.sender == owner, \"Not the Owner\");\n    _;\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Function that allows anyone to change the state variable \"greeting\" of the contract and increase the counters\n   *\n   * @param _newGreeting (string memory) - new greeting to save on the contract\n   */\n  function setGreeting(string memory _newGreeting) public payable {\n    // Print data to the anvil chain console. Remove when deploying to a live network.\n\n    console.logString(\"Setting new greeting\");\n    console.logString(_newGreeting);\n\n    greeting = _newGreeting;\n    totalCounter += 1;\n    userGreetingCounter[msg.sender] += 1;\n\n    // msg.value: built-in global variable that represents the amount of ether sent with the transaction\n    if (msg.value > 0) {\n      premium = true;\n    } else {\n      premium = false;\n    }\n\n    // emit: keyword used to trigger an event\n    emit GreetingChange(msg.sender, _newGreeting, msg.value > 0, msg.value);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Function that allows the owner to withdraw all the Ether in the contract\n   * The function can only be called by the owner of the contract as defined by the isOwner modifier\n   */\n  function withdraw() public isOwner {\n    (bool success,) = owner.call{ value: address(this).balance }(\"\");\n    require(success, \"Failed to send Ether\");\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Function that allows the contract to receive ETH\n   */\n  receive() external payable { }\n}\n=== Deploy.s.sol ===\n//SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.19;\n\nimport \"./DeployHelpers.s.sol\";\nimport { DeployYourContract } from \"./DeployYourContract.s.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @notice Main deployment script for all contracts\n * @dev Run this when you want to deploy multiple contracts at once\n *\n * Example: yarn deploy # runs this script(without`--file` flag)\n */\ncontract DeployScript is ScaffoldETHDeploy {\n  function run() external {\n    // Deploys all your contracts sequentially\n    // Add new deployments here when needed\n\n    \n    DeployYourContract deployYourContract = new DeployYourContract();\n    deployYourContract.run();\n\n\n    // Deploy another contract\n    // DeployMyContract myContract = new DeployMyContract();\n    // myContract.run();\n  }\n}=== DeployYourContract.s.sol ===\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.19;\n\nimport \"./DeployHelpers.s.sol\";\nimport \"../contracts/YourContract.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @notice Deploy script for YourContract contract\n * @dev Inherits ScaffoldETHDeploy which:\n *      - Includes forge-std/Script.sol for deployment\n *      - Includes ScaffoldEthDeployerRunner modifier\n *      - Provides `deployer` variable\n * Example:\n * yarn deploy --file DeployYourContract.s.sol  # {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMR1KvLj6ZXCo3A44PKK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Wj52BrCuEy4JjDf2nWRj6E","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T190912Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/packages/foundry/contracts/TipJar.sol","content":"//SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity >=0.8.0 <0.9.0;\n\nimport { IERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport { SafeERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @notice A USDC tip jar. Anyone can leave a USDC tip with a short message; the owner\n *         can withdraw the collected balance. Designed for Base (USDC has 6 decimals).\n * @dev Uses SafeERC20 so it works with tokens (like USDC) whose transfer* functions\n *      do not return a bool. The token address is injected at construction so the same\n *      contract can point at real Base USDC on a fork/mainnet or a mock in unit tests.\n */\ncontract TipJar {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\n    struct Tip {\n        address tipper;\n        uint256 amount;\n        uint256 timestamp;\n        string message;\n    }\n\n    IERC20 public immutable usdc;\n    address public immutable owner;\n\n    Tip[] private tips;\n    uint256 public totalTipped;\n    mapping(address => uint256) public tippedBy;\n\n    event NewTip(address indexed tipper, uint256 amount, string message, uint256 timestamp);\n    event Withdrawn(address indexed to, uint256 amount);\n\n    error NotOwner();\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error NothingToWithdraw();\n\n    modifier onlyOwner() {\n        if (msg.sender != owner) revert NotOwner();\n        _;\n    }\n\n    constructor(IERC20 _usdc, address _owner) {\n        usdc = _usdc;\n        owner = _owner;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Leave a USDC tip. Caller must have approved this contract for `amount` first.\n     * @param amount USDC amount in base units (6 decimals, e.g. 1 USDC = 1_000_000).\n     * @param message Short public message shown in the tip feed.\n     */\n    function tip(uint256 amount, string calldata message) external {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Pull the USDC in first, then record — reverts here roll back the whole tip.\n        usdc.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n\n        tips.push(Tip({ tipper: msg.sender, amount: amount, timestamp: block.timestamp, message: message }));\n        totalTipped += amount;\n        tippedBy[msg.sender] += amount;\n\n        emit NewTip(msg.sender, amount, message, block.timestamp);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Withdraw the full USDC balance to the owner.\n    function withdraw() external onlyOwner {\n        uint256 balance = usdc.balanceOf(address(this));\n        if (balance == 0) revert NothingToWithdraw();\n\n        usdc.safeTransfer(owner, balance);\n        emit Withdrawn(owner, balance);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of tips recorded so far.\n    function tipCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return tips.length;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Every tip, oldest first. The frontend reverses this for a newest-first feed.\n    function getTips() external view returns (Tip[] memory) {\n        return tips;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice The most recent `count` tips, newest first (cheap read for the feed).\n    function getRecentTips(uint256 count) external view returns (Tip[] memory recent) {\n        uint256 total = tips.length;\n        if (count > total) count = total;\n        recent = new Tip[](count);\n        for (uint256 i = 0; i < count; i++) {\n            recent[i] = tips[total - 1 - i];\n        }\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1257,"cache_read_input_tokens":55386,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1257},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883f155b-a7ed-4467-8dca-d277ae7a1ce9","uuid":"3ea0daef-8dd7-4889-bf22-08e4742f15dd","timestamp":"2026-07-24T19:13:28.288Z","request_id":"req_011CdMR1JrbVFQhpdLWrQTyW"}

Anyone can leave a USDC tip with a short message; the owner\n *         can withdraw the collected balance. Designed for Base (USDC has 6 decimals).\n * @dev Uses SafeERC20 so it works with tokens (like USDC) whose transfer* functions\n *      do not return a bool. The token address is injected at construction so the same\n *      contract can point at real Base USDC on a fork/mainnet or a mock in unit tests.\n */\ncontract TipJar {\n    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;\n\n    struct Tip {\n        address tipper;\n        uint256 amount;\n        uint256 timestamp;\n        string message;\n    }\n\n    IERC20 public immutable usdc;\n    address public immutable owner;\n\n    Tip[] private tips;\n    uint256 public totalTipped;\n    mapping(address => uint256) public tippedBy;\n\n    event NewTip(address indexed tipper, uint256 amount, string message, uint256 timestamp);\n    event Withdrawn(address indexed to, uint256 amount);\n\n    error NotOwner();\n    error ZeroAmount();\n    error NothingToWithdraw();\n\n    modifier onlyOwner() {\n        if (msg.sender != owner) revert NotOwner();\n        _;\n    }\n\n    constructor(IERC20 _usdc, address _owner) {\n        usdc = _usdc;\n        owner = _owner;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Leave a USDC tip. Caller must have approved this contract for `amount` first.\n     * @param amount USDC amount in base units (6 decimals, e.g. 1 USDC = 1_000_000).\n     * @param message Short public message shown in the tip feed.\n     */\n    function tip(uint256 amount, string calldata message) external {\n        if (amount == 0) revert ZeroAmount();\n\n        // Pull the USDC in first, then record — reverts here roll back the whole tip.\n        usdc.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);\n\n        tips.push(Tip({ tipper: msg.sender, amount: amount, timestamp: block.timestamp, message: message }));\n        totalTipped += amount;\n        tippedBy[msg.sender] += amount;\n\n        emit NewTip(msg.sender, amount, message, block.timestamp);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Withdraw the full USDC balance to the owner.\n    function withdraw() external onlyOwner {\n        uint256 balance = usdc.balanceOf(address(this));\n        if (balance == 0) revert NothingToWithdraw();\n\n        usdc.safeTransfer(owner, balance);\n        emit Withdrawn(owner, balance);\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Number of tips recorded so far.\n    function tipCount() external view returns (uint256) {\n        return tips.length;\n    }\n\n    /// @notice Every tip, oldest first. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMR4T8WcqbMQHSJu7ySW","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_015wkop4Zct1G1vtTrBFXnE7","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T190912Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/packages/foundry/test/TipJar.t.sol","content":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity >=0.8.0 <0.9.0;\n\nimport { Test } from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport { ERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol\";\nimport { IERC20 } from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport { TipJar } from \"../contracts/TipJar.sol\";\n\n/// @dev 6-decimal stand-in for USDC used in unit tests.\ncontract MockUSDC is ERC20 {\n    constructor() ERC20(\"Mock USD Coin\", \"USDC\") { }\n\n    function decimals() public pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return 6;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n}\n\ncontract TipJarTest is Test {\n    MockUSDC usdc;\n    TipJar jar;\n\n    address owner = makeAddr(\"owner\");\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    uint256 constant ONE_USDC = 1e6;\n\n    event NewTip(address indexed tipper, uint256 amount, string message, uint256 timestamp);\n    event Withdrawn(address indexed to, uint256 amount);\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdc = new MockUSDC();\n        jar = new TipJar(IERC20(address(usdc)), owner);\n        usdc.mint(alice, 1000 * ONE_USDC);\n        usdc.mint(bob, 1000 * ONE_USDC);\n    }\n\n    function _tip(address from, uint256 amount, string memory message) internal {\n        vm.startPrank(from);\n        usdc.approve(address(jar), amount);\n        jar.tip(amount, message);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_TipMovesUsdcAndRecordsFeed() public {\n        vm.expectEmit(true, false, false, true);\n        emit NewTip(alice, 5 * ONE_USDC, \"gm\", block.timestamp);\n        _tip(alice, 5 * ONE_USDC, \"gm\");\n\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(jar.tippedBy(alice), 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(jar.tipCount(), 1);\n\n        TipJar.Tip[] memory tips = jar.getTips();\n        assertEq(tips.length, 1);\n        assertEq(tips[0].tipper, alice);\n        assertEq(tips[0].amount, 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(tips[0].message, \"gm\");\n    }\n\n    function test_RecentTipsAreNewestFirst() public {\n        _tip(alice, 1 * ONE_USDC, \"first\");\n        _tip(bob, 2 * ONE_USDC, \"second\");\n        _tip(alice, 3 * ONE_USDC, \"third\");\n\n        TipJar.Tip[] memory recent = jar.getRecentTips(2);\n        assertEq(recent.length, 2);\n        assertEq(recent[0].message, \"third\");\n        assertEq(recent[1].message, \"second\");\n\n        // Asking for more than exist just returns everything.\n        assertEq(jar.getRecentTips(100).length, 3);\n    }\n\n    function test_TipRevertsOnZeroAmount() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        jar.tip(0, \"nope\");\n    }\n\n    function test_TipRevertsWithoutApproval() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        jar.tip(ONE_USDC, \"no allowance\");\n    }\n\n    function test_OwnerCanWithdraw() public {\n        _tip(alice, 10 * ONE_USDC, \"thanks\");\n\n        vm.expectEmit(true, false, false, true);\n        emit Withdrawn(owner, 10 * ONE_USDC);\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        jar.withdraw();\n\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(owner), 10 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawRevertsForNonOwner() public {\n        _tip(alice, ONE_USDC, \"hi\");\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.NotOwner.selector);\n        jar.withdraw();\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawRevertsWhenEmpty() public {\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.NothingToWithdraw.selector);\n        jar.withdraw();\n    }\n\n    function testFuzz_TipAccounting(uint96 a, uint96 b) public {\n        vm.assume(a > 0 && b > 0);\n        usdc.mint(alice, a);\n        usdc.mint(bob, b);\n\n        _tip(alice, a, \"a\");\n        _tip(bob, b, \"b\");\n\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), uint256(a) + b);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), uint256(a) + b);\n        assertEq(jar.tipCount(), 2);\n    }\n}\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":300,"cache_read_input_tokens":60657,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":300},"output_tokens":64,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883f155b-a7ed-4467-8dca-d277ae7a1ce9","uuid":"f2b486d3-f124-47f6-bbb8-f7010283400b","timestamp":"2026-07-24T19:14:12.565Z","request_id":"req_011CdMR4QzGtS6cYXVzN14G3"}

constructor() ERC20(\"Mock USD Coin\", \"USDC\") { }\n\n    function decimals() public pure override returns (uint8) {\n        return 6;\n    }\n\n    function mint(address to, uint256 amount) external {\n        _mint(to, amount);\n    }\n}\n\ncontract TipJarTest is Test {\n    MockUSDC usdc;\n    TipJar jar;\n\n    address owner = makeAddr(\"owner\");\n    address alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    uint256 constant ONE_USDC = 1e6;\n\n    event NewTip(address indexed tipper, uint256 amount, string message, uint256 timestamp);\n    event Withdrawn(address indexed to, uint256 amount);\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        usdc = new MockUSDC();\n        jar = new TipJar(IERC20(address(usdc)), owner);\n        usdc.mint(alice, 1000 * ONE_USDC);\n        usdc.mint(bob, 1000 * ONE_USDC);\n    }\n\n    function _tip(address from, uint256 amount, string memory message) internal {\n        vm.startPrank(from);\n        usdc.approve(address(jar), amount);\n        jar.tip(amount, message);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function test_TipMovesUsdcAndRecordsFeed() public {\n        vm.expectEmit(true, false, false, true);\n        emit NewTip(alice, 5 * ONE_USDC, \"gm\", block.timestamp);\n        _tip(alice, 5 * ONE_USDC, \"gm\");\n\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(jar.tippedBy(alice), 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(jar.tipCount(), 1);\n\n        TipJar.Tip[] memory tips = jar.getTips();\n        assertEq(tips.length, 1);\n        assertEq(tips[0].tipper, alice);\n        assertEq(tips[0].amount, 5 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(tips[0].message, \"gm\");\n    }\n\n    function test_RecentTipsAreNewestFirst() public {\n        _tip(alice, 1 * ONE_USDC, \"first\");\n        _tip(bob, 2 * ONE_USDC, \"second\");\n        _tip(alice, 3 * ONE_USDC, \"third\");\n\n        TipJar.Tip[] memory recent = jar.getRecentTips(2);\n        assertEq(recent.length, 2);\n        assertEq(recent[0].message, \"third\");\n        assertEq(recent[1].message, \"second\");\n\n        // Asking for more than exist just returns everything.\n        assertEq(jar.getRecentTips(100).length, 3);\n    }\n\n    function test_TipRevertsOnZeroAmount() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.ZeroAmount.selector);\n        jar.tip(0, \"nope\");\n    }\n\n    function test_TipRevertsWithoutApproval() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        jar.tip(ONE_USDC, \"no allowance\");\n    }\n\n    function test_OwnerCanWithdraw() public {\n        _tip(alice, 10 * ONE_USDC, \"thanks\");\n\n        vm.expectEmit(true, false, false, true);\n        emit Withdrawn(owner, 10 * ONE_USDC);\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        jar.withdraw();\n\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(owner), 10 * ONE_USDC);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), 0);\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawRevertsForNonOwner() public {\n        _tip(alice, ONE_USDC, \"hi\");\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.NotOwner.selector);\n        jar.withdraw();\n    }\n\n    function test_WithdrawRevertsWhenEmpty() public {\n        vm.prank(owner);\n        vm.expectRevert(TipJar.NothingToWithdraw.selector);\n        jar.withdraw();\n    }\n\n    function testFuzz_TipAccounting(uint96 a, uint96 b) public {\n        vm.assume(a > 0 && b > 0);\n        usdc.mint(alice, a);\n        usdc.mint(bob, b);\n\n        _tip(alice, a, \"a\");\n        _tip(bob, b, \"b\");\n\n        assertEq(jar.totalTipped(), uint256(a) + b);\n        assertEq(usdc.balanceOf(address(jar)), uint256(a) + b);\n        assertEq(jar.tipCount(), 2);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":47,"oldLines":9,"newStart":47,"newLines":12,"lines":[" {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMR8W7xThwYTDvPBBcyS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_016MYMzeQNBmJoeHksw8RU34","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T190912Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n#\n# Seed test identities with REAL Base USDC on the local fork.\n#\n# Why this is safe: everything runs against a local Anvil fork of Base (chain id\n# 31337). The USDC contract's real bytecode and state are copied from Base, but any\n# writes stay local — no transaction ever touches Base mainnet, so no real money is\n# at risk. We use USDC's own masterMinter (impersonated on the fork) to mint fresh\n# balances, so seeding never depends on any whale's balance.\n#\n# Usage (fork must already be running via `yarn fork --network base`):\n#   bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh [address ...]\n#\n#   # no args -> seeds Anvil's default accounts #0 and #1\n#   bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh\n#\n#   # seed a specific wallet (e.g. the burner address shown in the app)\n#   bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh 0xYourBurnerAddress\n#\n# Env:\n#   RPC     RPC url of the fork          (default http://127.0.0.1:8545)\n#   AMOUNT  USDC per account, base units (default 1000000000 = 1,000 USDC)\nset -euo pipefail\n\nRPC=\"${RPC:-http://127.0.0.1:8545}\"\nUSDC=\"0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\"\nAMOUNT=\"${AMOUNT:-1000000000}\" # 1,000 USDC (6 decimals)\nONE_ETH=\"0xDE0B6B3A7640000\" # 1 ETH in wei, for gas\n\n# Anvil's first two deterministic accounts (private keys are public knowledge —\n# perfect throwaway \"test identities\" for a demo).\nDEFAULT_ACCOUNTS=(\n  \"0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266\"\n  \"0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8\"\n)\n\nif [ \"$#\" -gt 0 ]; then\n  ACCOUNTS=(\"$@\")\nelse\n  ACCOUNTS=(\"${DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS[@]}\")\nfi\n\necho \"Fork RPC: $RPC\"\nif ! cast chain-id --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n  echo \"❌ Can't reach the fork at $RPC. Start it first: yarn fork --network base\" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\n\n# The masterMinter can authorize new minters. We impersonate it, make Anvil account #0\n# a minter, then mint USDC from #0 to every target account.\nMINTER=\"${DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS[0]}\"\nMASTER=\"$(cast call \"$USDC\" \"masterMinter()(address)\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\")\"\necho \"USDC masterMinter: $MASTER\"\n\n# Fund the accounts that need to send txs with gas money.\nfor a in \"$MASTER\" \"$MINTER\" \"${ACCOUNTS[@]}\"; do\n  cast rpc anvil_setBalance \"$a\" \"$ONE_ETH\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\ndone\n\ncast rpc anvil_impersonateAccount \"$MASTER\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\ncast send \"$USDC\" \"configureMinter(address,uint256)\" \"$MINTER\" \\\n  1000000000000000 --from \"$MASTER\" --unlocked --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\ncast rpc anvil_stopImpersonatingAccount \"$MASTER\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\n\ncast rpc anvil_impersonateAccount \"$MINTER\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\nfor a in \"${ACCOUNTS[@]}\"; do\n  cast send \"$USDC\" \"mint(address,uint256)\" \"$a\" \"$AMOUNT\" \\\n    --from \"$MINTER\" --unlocked --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\ndone\ncast rpc anvil_stopImpersonatingAccount \"$MINTER\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\n\necho \"Seeded (USDC base units, 6 decimals):\"\nfor a in \"${ACCOUNTS[@]}\"; do\n  bal=\"$(cast call \"$USDC\" \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" \"$a\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\")\"\n  echo \"  $a -> ${bal%% *}\"\ndone\necho \"Done. These identities can now send tips on the local fork.\"\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":369,"cache_read_input_tokens":66442,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":369},"output_tokens":56,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883f155b-a7ed-4467-8dca-d277ae7a1ce9","uuid":"922a63fc-adcd-4c0f-b47d-c357c1ff6e38","timestamp":"2026-07-24T19:15:11.334Z","request_id":"req_011CdMR8UQmEQeuprEoMSh7S"}

The USDC contract's real bytecode and state are copied from Base, but any\n# writes stay local — no transaction ever touches Base mainnet, so no real money is\n# at risk. We use USDC's own masterMinter (impersonated on the fork) to mint fresh\n# balances, so seeding never depends on any whale's balance.\n#\n# Usage (fork must already be running via `yarn fork --network base`):\n#   bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh [address ...]\n#\n#   # no args -> seeds Anvil's default accounts #0 and #1\n#   bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh\n#\n#   # seed a specific wallet (e.g. the burner address shown in the app)\n#   bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh 0xYourBurnerAddress\n#\n# Env:\n#   RPC     RPC url of the fork          (default http://127.0.0.1:8545)\n#   AMOUNT  USDC per account, base units (default 1000000000 = 1,000 USDC)\nset -euo pipefail\n\nRPC=\"${RPC:-http://127.0.0.1:8545}\"\nUSDC=\"0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\"\nAMOUNT=\"${AMOUNT:-1000000000}\" # 1,000 USDC (6 decimals)\nONE_ETH=\"0xDE0B6B3A7640000\" # 1 ETH in wei, for gas\n\n# Anvil's first two deterministic accounts (private keys are public knowledge —\n# perfect throwaway \"test identities\" for a demo).\nDEFAULT_ACCOUNTS=(\n  \"0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266\"\n  \"0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8\"\n)\n\nif [ \"$#\" -gt 0 ]; then\n  ACCOUNTS=(\"$@\")\nelse\n  ACCOUNTS=(\"${DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS[@]}\")\nfi\n\necho \"Fork RPC: $RPC\"\nif ! cast chain-id --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n  echo \"❌ Can't reach the fork at $RPC. Start it first: yarn fork --network base\" >&2\n  exit 1\nfi\n\n# The masterMinter can authorize new minters. We impersonate it, make Anvil account #0\n# a minter, then mint USDC from #0 to every target account.\nMINTER=\"${DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS[0]}\"\nMASTER=\"$(cast call \"$USDC\" \"masterMinter()(address)\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\")\"\necho \"USDC masterMinter: $MASTER\"\n\n# Fund the accounts that need to send txs with gas money.\nfor a in \"$MASTER\" \"$MINTER\" \"${ACCOUNTS[@]}\"; do\n  cast rpc anvil_setBalance \"$a\" \"$ONE_ETH\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\ndone\n\ncast rpc anvil_impersonateAccount \"$MASTER\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\ncast send \"$USDC\" \"configureMinter(address,uint256)\" \"$MINTER\" \\\n  1000000000000000 --from \"$MASTER\" --unlocked --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\ncast rpc anvil_stopImpersonatingAccount \"$MASTER\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\n\ncast rpc anvil_impersonateAccount \"$MINTER\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\nfor a in \"${ACCOUNTS[@]}\"; do\n  cast send \"$USDC\" \"mint(address,uint256)\" \"$a\" \"$AMOUNT\" \\\n    --from \"$MINTER\" --unlocked --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\ndone\ncast rpc anvil_stopImpersonatingAccount \"$MINTER\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\" >/dev/null\n\necho \"Seeded (USDC base units, 6 decimals):\"\nfor a in \"${ACCOUNTS[@]}\"; do\n  bal=\"$(cast call \"$USDC\" \"balanceOf(address)(uint256)\" \"$a\" --rpc-url \"$RPC\")\"\n  echo \"  $a -> ${bal%% *}\"\ndone\necho \"Done. These identities can now send tips on the local fork.\"\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01URhEwz89TUxxQ4JC7QEpqv","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2\n2\t\n3\t<h4 align=\"center\">\n4\t  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |\n5\t  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>\n6\t</h4>\n7\t\n8\t🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. It's designed to make it easier for developers to create and deploy smart contracts and build user interfaces that interact with those contracts.\n9\t\n10\t> [!NOTE]\n11\t> 🤖 Scaffold-ETH 2 is AI-ready! It has everything agents need to build on Ethereum. Check `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode` or `.cursor/` for more info.\n12\t\n13\t⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n14\t\n15\t- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n16\t- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: Collection of React hooks wrapper around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) to simplify interactions with smart contracts with typescript autocompletion.\n17\t- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Collection of common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n18\t- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test your application with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n19\t- 🔐 **Integration with Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers and interact with the Ethereum network.\n20\t\n21\t![Debug Contracts tab](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/assets/55535804/b237af0c-5027-4849-a5c1-2e31495cccb1)\n22\t\n23\t## Requirements\n24\t\n25\tBefore you begin, you need to install the following tools:\n26\t\n27\t- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n28\t- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n29\t- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n30\t\n31\t## Quickstart\n32\t\n33\tTo get started with Scaffold-ETH 2, follow the steps below:\n34\t\n35\t1. Install dependencies if it was skipped in CLI:\n36\t\n37\t```\n38\tcd my-dapp-example\n39\tyarn install\n40\t```\n41\t\n42\t2. Run a local network in the first terminal:\n43\t\n44\t```\n45\tyarn chain\n46\t```\n47\t\n48\tThis command starts a local Ethereum network using Foundry. The network runs on your local machine and can be used for testing and development. You can customize the network configuration in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`.\n49\t\n50\t3. On a second terminal, deploy the test contract:\n51\t\n52\t```\n53\tyarn deploy\n54\t```\n55\t\n56\tThis command deploys a test smart contract to the local network. The contract is located in `packages/foundry/contracts` and can be modified to suit your needs. The `yarn deploy` command uses the deploy script located in `packages/foundry/script` to deploy the contract to the network. You can also customize the deploy script.\n57\t\n58\t4. On a third terminal, start your NextJS app:\n59\t\n60\t```\n61\tyarn start\n62\t```\n63\t\n64\tVisit your app on: `http://localhost:3000`. You can interact with your smart contract using the `Debug Contracts` page. You can tweak the app config in `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts`.\n65\t\n66\tRun smart contract test with `yarn foundry:test`\n67\t\n68\t- Edit your smart contracts in `packages/foundry/contracts`\n69\t- Edit your frontend homepage at `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx`. For guidance on [routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/defining-routes) and configuring [pages/layouts](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts) checkout the Next.js documentation.\n70\t- Edit your deployment scripts in `packages/foundry/script`\n71\t\n72\t\n73\t## Documentation\n74\t\n75\tVisit our [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn how to start building with Scaffold-ETH 2.\n76\t\n77\tTo know more about its features, check out our [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n78\t\n79\t## Contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2\n80\t\n81\tWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2!\n82\t\n83\tPlease see [CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information and guidelines for contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883f155b-a7ed-4467-8dca-d277ae7a1ce9","uuid":"5fb50aa9-3af9-4ebe-b979-dea565e20599","timestamp":"2026-07-24T19:24:45.501Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T190912Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/README.md","content":"# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2\n\n<h4 align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |\n  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>\n</h4>\n\n🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. It's designed to make it easier for developers to create and deploy smart contracts and build user interfaces that interact with those contracts.\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 Scaffold-ETH 2 is AI-ready! It has everything agents need to build on Ethereum. Check `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode` or `.cursor/` for more info.\n\n⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n\n- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: Collection of React hooks wrapper around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) to simplify interactions with smart contracts with typescript autocompletion.\n- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Collection of common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test your application with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n- 🔐 **Integration with Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers and interact with the Ethereum network.\n\n![Debug Contracts tab](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/assets/55535804/b237af0c-5027-4849-a5c1-2e31495cccb1)\n\n## Requirements\n\nBefore you begin, you need to install the following tools:\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\n## Quickstart\n\nTo get started with Scaffold-ETH 2, follow the steps below:\n\n1. Install dependencies if it was skipped in CLI:\n\n```\ncd my-dapp-example\nyarn install\n```\n\n2. Run a local network in the first terminal:\n\n```\nyarn chain\n```\n\nThis command starts a local Ethereum network using Foundry. The network runs on your local machine and can be used for testing and development. You can customize the network configuration in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`.\n\n3. On a second terminal, deploy the test contract:\n\n```\nyarn deploy\n```\n\nThis command deploys a test smart contract to the local network. The contract is located in `packages/foundry/contracts` and can be modified to suit your needs. The `yarn deploy` command uses the deploy script located in `packages/foundry/script` to deploy the contract to the network. You can also customize the deploy script.\n\n4. On a third terminal, start your NextJS app:\n\n```\nyarn start\n```\n\nVisit your app on: `http://localhost:3000`. You can interact with your smart contract using the `Debug Contracts` page. You can tweak the app config in `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts`.\n\nRun smart contract test with `yarn foundry:test`\n\n- Edit your smart contracts in `packages/foundry/contracts`\n- Edit your frontend homepage at `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx`. For guidance on [routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/defining-routes) and configuring [pages/layouts](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts) checkout the Next.js documentation.\n- Edit your deployment scripts in `packages/foundry/script`\n\n\n## Documentation\n\nVisit our [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn how to start building with Scaffold-ETH 2.\n\nTo know more about its features, check out our [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n\n## Contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2\n\nWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2!\n\nPlease see [CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information and guidelines for contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2.","numLines":83,"startLine":1,"totalLines":83}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMRtYjgypzAd4VbhhGrF","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_0193ZbkZstgarFbxQnMZ79C1","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T190912Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/README.md","content":"# USDC Tip Jar (Base)\n\nA tiny dApp where anyone can leave a **USDC tip** with a short message, and the owner can\nwithdraw the collected balance. Built on [Scaffold-ETH 2](https://scaffoldeth.io) (Foundry\nflavor) for **Base**.\n\n- **Contract:** `packages/foundry/contracts/TipJar.sol` — pulls USDC via `transferFrom`\n  (SafeERC20), records each tip + message, lets the owner withdraw.\n- **Frontend:** `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx` — a live tip feed plus an approve → tip form.\n- **USDC on Base:** `0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913` (6 decimals).\n\nThe whole thing is developed and demoed **locally against a fork of real Base**, so tips move\nreal USDC between test identities without any real money at risk. It ships as a **static build\non IPFS** — see [`DEPLOY.md`](./DEPLOY.md).\n\n---\n\n## Requirements\n\n- [Node >= v20.18.3](https://nodejs.org/en/download/) (Node 23+ works too — see the note below)\n- [Yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/)\n- [Foundry](https://book.getfoundry.sh/getting-started/installation) (`anvil` + `cast` on your PATH)\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\n> **Node 23+ note:** newer Node ships a broken global `localStorage`. This repo already\n> compensates (a polyfill is `--require`d by the `dev`, `start`, and IPFS build scripts), so\n> `yarn start` and the production build work on Node 20–25 alike. Nothing extra to do.\n\n```bash\nyarn install\n```\n\n---\n\n## Local demo workflow (against real Base state)\n\nEverything below runs on a **local Anvil fork of Base** (chain id `31337`). The fork copies\nBase's real state — including the real USDC contract — but every transaction stays on your\nmachine. **No transaction ever touches Base mainnet, so no real money is at risk.** We mint\nUSDC to throwaway \"test identities\" using USDC's own minter (impersonated on the fork), then\nsend tips between them.\n\nUse three terminals.\n\n### Terminal 1 — fork Base\n\n```bash\nyarn fork\n```\n\nThis runs `anvil --fork-url base --chain-id 31337 --block-time 1`, forking Base from\n`foundry.toml`'s `base` RPC. `--block-time 1` mines a block per second so tip timestamps\nadvance. Leave it running.\n\n### Terminal 2 — deploy the TipJar to the fork\n\n```bash\nyarn deploy\n```\n\nDeploys `TipJar` pointing at the real Base USDC address and writes its ABI/address to\n`packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts`.\n\n### Seed test identities with real USDC\n\nWith the fork running, give your test wallets USDC (and some ETH for gas):\n\n```bash\n# Default: seeds Anvil accounts #0 and #1 with 1,000 USDC each\nbash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh\n\n# Or seed a specific wallet (e.g. the burner address the app shows you)\nbash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh 0xYourWalletAddress\n\n# Custom amount (base units, 6 decimals). 5,000 USDC:\nAMOUNT=5000000000 bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh 0xAlice 0xBob\n```\n\nThe script impersonates USDC's `masterMinter` on the fork, authorizes a minter, and mints\nfresh USDC to each address — so it never depends on any whale's balance.\n\n**Test identities.** The two defaults are Anvil's deterministic accounts, whose private keys\nare public and perfect as throwaways:\n\n| Account | Address | Private key |\n| ------- | ------- | ----------- |\n| #0 | `0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266` | `0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80` |\n| #1 | `0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8` | `0x59c6995e998f97a5a0044966f0945389dc9e86dae88c7a8412f4603b6b78690d` |\n\nImport a key into MetaMask/Rainbow (add a custom network: RPC `http://127.0.0.1:8545`,\nchain id `31337`), or just use the built-in **burner wallet** the app shows on the local\nnetwork and seed that address.\n\n### Terminal 3 — run the frontend\n\n```bash\nyarn start\n```\n\nOpen http://localhost:3000. The app targets the local fork (`chains.foundry`, id `31337`) —\nsee `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts`.\n\n### Demo a tip\n\n1. Connect wallet (or use the burner). Make sure that address was seeded above.\n2. Enter an amount (e.g. `2.5`) and a message.\n3. First tip needs a one-time **Approve** (USDC allowance), then **Send tip**.\n4. Watch the **Tip feed** and the **Total tipped / In the jar** stats update — that's real\n   USDC moving on the fork.\n5. As the owner (the deployer, Anvil account #9), call `withdraw()` from the **Debug\n   Contracts** page to pull the balance out.\n\nYou can also drive it entirely from the CLI:\n\n```bash\nJAR=$(grep -o '0x[a-fA-F0-9]\\{40\\}' packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts | head -1)\nUSDC=0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913\nPK=0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80  # Anvil #0\ncast send $USDC \"approve(address,uint256)\" $JAR 2500000 --private-key $PK --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:8545\ncast send $JAR \"tip(uint256,string)\" 2500000 \"gm from the cli\" --private-key $PK --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:8545\ncast call $JAR \"getRecentTips(uint256)((address,uint256,uint256,string)[])\" 5 --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:8545\n```\n\n---\n\n## Tests\n\n```bash\nyarn foundry:test          # unit + fuzz tests for TipJar\n```\n\n---\n\n## Deploying\n\n- **Frontend → IPFS static build:** [`DEPLOY.md`](./DEPLOY.md).\n- **Contract → real Base:** `yarn deploy --file DeployTipJar.s.sol --network base` (requires a\n  funded keystore account; see `yarn account`).\n\n---\n\n## Built with Scaffold-ETH 2\n\nThis project is scaffolded with [Scaffold-ETH 2](https://scaffoldeth.io) — NextJS, RainbowKit,\nFoundry, Wagmi, Viem, and TypeScript. See the [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1851,"cache_read_input_tokens":117769,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1851},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883f155b-a7ed-4467-8dca-d277ae7a1ce9","uuid":"3e56a6aa-d8b6-49a6-ab4e-a19d6af1498e","timestamp":"2026-07-24T19:25:26.825Z","request_id":"req_011CdMRtXABioy8qBYwW9L6P"}

On a second terminal, deploy the test contract:","+Use three terminals."," ","+### Terminal 1 — fork Base","+","+```bash","+yarn fork"," ```","+","+This runs `anvil --fork-url base --chain-id 31337 --block-time 1`, forking Base from","+`foundry.toml`'s `base` RPC. `--block-time 1` mines a block per second so tip timestamps","+advance. On a third terminal, start your NextJS app:","+### Seed test identities with real USDC"," ","+With the fork running, give your test wallets USDC (and some ETH for gas):","+","+```bash","+# Default: seeds Anvil accounts #0 and #1 with 1,000 USDC each","+bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh","+","+# Or seed a specific wallet (e.g. the burner address the app shows you)","+bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh 0xYourWalletAddress","+","+# Custom amount (base units, 6 decimals). 5,000 USDC:","+AMOUNT=5000000000 bash packages/foundry/scripts-js/seed-usdc.sh 0xAlice 0xBob"," ```","+","+The script impersonates USDC's `masterMinter` on the fork, authorizes a minter, and mints","+fresh USDC to each address — so it never depends on any whale's balance.","+","+**Test identities.** The two defaults are Anvil's deterministic accounts, whose private keys","+are public and perfect as throwaways:","+","+| Account | Address | Private key |","+| ------- | ------- | ----------- |","+| #0 | `0xf39Fd6e51aad88F6F4ce6aB8827279cffFb92266` | `0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80` |","+| #1 | `0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8` | `0x59c6995e998f97a5a0044966f0945389dc9e86dae88c7a8412f4603b6b78690d` |","+","+Import a key into MetaMask/Rainbow (add a custom network: RPC `http://127.0.0.1:8545`,","+chain id `31337`), or just use the built-in **burner wallet** the app shows on the local","+network and seed that address.","+","+### Terminal 3 — run the frontend","+","+```bash"," yarn start"," ```"," ","-Visit your app on: `http://localhost:3000`. For guidance on [routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/defining-routes) and configuring [pages/layouts](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts) checkout the Next.js documentation.","-- Edit your deployment scripts in `packages/foundry/script`","+1. Watch the **Tip feed** and the **Total tipped / In the jar** stats update — that's real","+   USDC moving on the fork.","+5. As the owner (the deployer, Anvil account #9), call `withdraw()` from the **Debug","+   Contracts** page to pull the balance out."," ","+You can also drive it entirely from the CLI:"," ","-## Documentation","+```bash","+JAR=$(grep -o '0x[a-fA-F0-9]\\{40\\}' packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts | head -1)","+USDC=0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913","+PK=0xac0974bec39a17e36ba4a6b4d238ff944bacb478cbed5efcae784d7bf4f2ff80  # Anvil #0","+cast send $USDC \"approve(address,uint256)\" $JAR 2500000 --private-key $PK --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:8545","+cast send $JAR \"tip(uint256,string)\" 2500000 \"gm from the cli\" --private-key $PK --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:8545","+cast call $JAR \"getRecentTips(uint256)((address,uint256,uint256,string)[])\" 5 --rpc-url http://127.0.0.1:8545","+```"," ","-Visit our [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn how to start building with Scaffold-ETH 2.","+---"," ","-To know more about its features, check out our [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).","+## Tests"," ","-## Contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2","+```bash","+yarn foundry:test          # unit + fuzz tests for TipJar","+```"," ","-We welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2!","+---"," ","-Please see [CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information and guidelines for contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2.","\\ No newline at end of file","+## Deploying","+","+- **Frontend → IPFS static build:** [`DEPLOY.md`](./DEPLOY.md).","+- **Contract → real Base:** `yarn deploy --file DeployTipJar.s.sol --network base` (requires a","+  funded keystore account; see `yarn account`).","+","+---","+","+## Built with Scaffold-ETH 2","+","+This project is scaffolded with [Scaffold-ETH 2](https://scaffoldeth.io) — NextJS, RainbowKit,","+Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and TypeScript. See the [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io)."]}],"originalFile":"# 🏗 Scaffold-ETH 2\n\n<h4 align=\"center\">\n  <a href=\"https://docs.scaffoldeth.io\">Documentation</a> |\n  <a href=\"https://scaffoldeth.io\">Website</a>\n</h4>\n\n🧪 An open-source, up-to-date toolkit for building decentralized applications (dapps) on the Ethereum blockchain. It's designed to make it easier for developers to create and deploy smart contracts and build user interfaces that interact with those contracts.\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> 🤖 Scaffold-ETH 2 is AI-ready! It has everything agents need to build on Ethereum. Check `.agents/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode` or `.cursor/` for more info.\n\n⚙️ Built using NextJS, RainbowKit, Foundry, Wagmi, Viem, and Typescript.\n\n- ✅ **Contract Hot Reload**: Your frontend auto-adapts to your smart contract as you edit it.\n- 🪝 **[Custom hooks](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/hooks/)**: Collection of React hooks wrapper around [wagmi](https://wagmi.sh/) to simplify interactions with smart contracts with typescript autocompletion.\n- 🧱 [**Components**](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/components/): Collection of common web3 components to quickly build your frontend.\n- 🔥 **Burner Wallet & Local Faucet**: Quickly test your application with a burner wallet and local faucet.\n- 🔐 **Integration with Wallet Providers**: Connect to different wallet providers and interact with the Ethereum network.\n\n![Debug Contracts tab](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/assets/55535804/b237af0c-5027-4849-a5c1-2e31495cccb1)\n\n## Requirements\n\nBefore you begin, you need to install the following tools:\n\n- [Node (>= v20.18.3)](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\n- Yarn ([v1](https://classic.yarnpkg.com/en/docs/install/) or [v2+](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install))\n- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)\n\n## Quickstart\n\nTo get started with Scaffold-ETH 2, follow the steps below:\n\n1. Install dependencies if it was skipped in CLI:\n\n```\ncd my-dapp-example\nyarn install\n```\n\n2. Run a local network in the first terminal:\n\n```\nyarn chain\n```\n\nThis command starts a local Ethereum network using Foundry. The network runs on your local machine and can be used for testing and development. You can customize the network configuration in `packages/foundry/foundry.toml`.\n\n3. On a second terminal, deploy the test contract:\n\n```\nyarn deploy\n```\n\nThis command deploys a test smart contract to the local network. The contract is located in `packages/foundry/contracts` and can be modified to suit your needs. The `yarn deploy` command uses the deploy script located in `packages/foundry/script` to deploy the contract to the network. You can also customize the deploy script.\n\n4. On a third terminal, start your NextJS app:\n\n```\nyarn start\n```\n\nVisit your app on: `http://localhost:3000`. You can interact with your smart contract using the `Debug Contracts` page. You can tweak the app config in `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts`.\n\nRun smart contract test with `yarn foundry:test`\n\n- Edit your smart contracts in `packages/foundry/contracts`\n- Edit your frontend homepage at `packages/nextjs/app/page.tsx`. For guidance on [routing](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/defining-routes) and configuring [pages/layouts](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts) checkout the Next.js documentation.\n- Edit your deployment scripts in `packages/foundry/script`\n\n\n## Documentation\n\nVisit our [docs](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io) to learn how to start building with Scaffold-ETH 2.\n\nTo know more about its features, check out our [website](https://scaffoldeth.io).\n\n## Contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2\n\nWe welcome contributions to Scaffold-ETH 2!\n\nPlease see [CONTRIBUTING.MD](https://github.com/scaffold-eth/scaffold-eth-2/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for more information and guidelines for contributing to Scaffold-ETH 2.","userModified":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdMRwbHZob2uKrDzZPkx6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01FYKszm7qmZ7AzsfRT8yiSy","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/spencerfaber/dev/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-playbook-goal-001/2026-07-24T190912Z-claude-with-skill-3/workspace/DEPLOY.md","content":"# Deploy — static build on IPFS\n\nThe frontend ships as a **static export** hosted on **IPFS**. Nothing is uploaded by this repo;\nthis document is the exact command list to build the site, upload it, and verify the result.\n\nThe production config is already in place:\n\n- `packages/nextjs/next.config.ts` — when `NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true`, sets\n  `output: \"export\"`, `trailingSlash: true` (so IPFS gateways resolve `/debug/` →\n  `debug/index.html` instead of 404), and unoptimized images.\n- `packages/nextjs/polyfill-localstorage.cjs` — restores the standard `localStorage` API that\n  Node 23+ ships broken, so prerendering doesn't crash. It's injected via\n  `NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\"` (works in every build worker, unlike\n  `instrumentation.ts` / `next.config`).\n- `utils/scaffold-eth/getMetadata.ts` — reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL` so the OG image\n  resolves to an absolute production URL (not `localhost`).\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- The contract is deployed to **real Base** and `packages/nextjs/contracts/deployedContracts.ts`\n  contains its Base (`8453`) entry:\n  ```bash\n  yarn deploy --file DeployTipJar.s.sol --network base\n  ```\n- `packages/nextjs/scaffold.config.ts` `targetNetworks` includes `chains.base` for the\n  production build (use `chains.foundry` only for local fork dev).\n- Use **Node 20 or 22** if you can; the polyfill also makes Node 23–25 work.\n\n## 1. Clean + build (static export)\n\nRun from `packages/nextjs`. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL` to your final gateway/ENS URL.\n\n```bash\ncd packages/nextjs\nrm -rf .next out                      # ALWAYS clean first — avoids shipping a stale build\n\nNEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL=\"https://tipjar.yourname.eth.link\" \\\n  NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\" \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true \\\n  NEXT_PUBLIC_IGNORE_BUILD_ERROR=true \\\n  yarn build\n```\n\n## 2. Verify the build BEFORE uploading\n\n```bash\n# Every route exists as a directory with an index.html (trailingSlash working):\nls out/index.html out/debug/index.html\n\n# OG image points at the production URL, not localhost:\ngrep -o 'og:image[^>]*' out/index.html\n\n# The app actually rendered (not an empty shell):\ngrep -o 'USDC Tip Jar' out/index.html\n\n# Build is fresh: out/ must be newer than your source.\nstat -f '%Sm' app/page.tsx\nstat -f '%Sm' out\n```\n\n## 3. Upload to IPFS\n\n```bash\n# From packages/nextjs\nyarn bgipfs upload out\n# → note the CID it prints. SAVE IT.\n```\n\nPreview it: `https://community.bgipfs.com/ipfs/<CID>`\n\n> The CID is proof of a fresh deploy: a real code change **always** produces a new CID. If the\n> CID didn't change, you uploaded stale output — re-run step 1.\n\n## 4. Post-deploy verification\n\n```bash\nCID=<your-cid>\nGATEWAY=https://community.bgipfs.com\n\n# Home + a nested route both return 200 (nested route proves trailingSlash routing):\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"home:  %{http_code}\\n\" -L \"$GATEWAY/ipfs/$CID/\"\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"debug: %{http_code}\\n\" -L \"$GATEWAY/ipfs/$CID/debug/\"\n\n# OG metadata resolves to the production URL:\ncurl -s -L \"$GATEWAY/ipfs/$CID/\" | grep -o 'og:image[^>]*'\n```\n\nThen open the preview URL in a browser and do a real walkthrough: connect wallet, confirm it\nprompts to switch to **Base**, approve USDC, send a tip, and watch the feed update.\n\n## 5. (Optional) Point an ENS subdomain at the CID\n\n1. `https://app.ens.domains/yourname.eth` → **Subnames** → **New subname** → e.g. `tipjar`\n   (skip this if the subname already exists).\n2. Open `https://app.ens.domains/tipjar.yourname.eth` → **Records** → **Edit Records** →\n   **Other** → set **Content Hash** to `ipfs://<CID>` → save + confirm in wallet.\n3. Verify onchain + via gateway (allow a few minutes for propagation):\n\n```bash\nNODE=$(cast namehash tipjar.yourname.eth)\nRESOLVER=$(cast call 0x00000000000C2e074eC69A0dFb2997BA6C7d2e1e \\\n  \"resolver(bytes32)(address)\" $NODE --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com)\ncast call $RESOLVER \"contenthash(bytes32)(bytes)\" $NODE --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com\n\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" -L \"https://tipjar.yourname.eth.link\"\n```\n\nUse `.eth.link` (better mobile support than `.eth.limo`).\n\n---\n\n### One-shot build + upload\n\nThe repo also wires `yarn ipfs` (from the repo root or `packages/nextjs`) to build with\n`NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true` and upload in one step. Prefer the explicit steps above when you\nneed `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL` and the localStorage polyfill set for correct OG metadata and\nprerendering.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2787,"cache_read_input_tokens":119620,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2787},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883f155b-a7ed-4467-8dca-d277ae7a1ce9","uuid":"384ae91c-b815-4cd0-ad91-a72521e85eb5","timestamp":"2026-07-24T19:26:00.061Z","request_id":"req_011CdMRwZiK1s48GLy7WAkpm"}

SAVE IT.\n```\n\nPreview it: `https://community.bgipfs.com/ipfs/<CID>`\n\n> The CID is proof of a fresh deploy: a real code change **always** produces a new CID. Post-deploy verification\n\n```bash\nCID=<your-cid>\nGATEWAY=https://community.bgipfs.com\n\n# Home + a nested route both return 200 (nested route proves trailingSlash routing):\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"home:  %{http_code}\\n\" -L \"$GATEWAY/ipfs/$CID/\"\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"debug: %{http_code}\\n\" -L \"$GATEWAY/ipfs/$CID/debug/\"\n\n# OG metadata resolves to the production URL:\ncurl -s -L \"$GATEWAY/ipfs/$CID/\" | grep -o 'og:image[^>]*'\n```\n\nThen open the preview URL in a browser and do a real walkthrough: connect wallet, confirm it\nprompts to switch to **Base**, approve USDC, send a tip, and watch the feed update.\n\n## 5. (Optional) Point an ENS subdomain at the CID\n\n1. `https://app.ens.domains/yourname.eth` → **Subnames** → **New subname** → e.g. `tipjar`\n   (skip this if the subname already exists).\n2. Open `https://app.ens.domains/tipjar.yourname.eth` → **Records** → **Edit Records** →\n   **Other** → set **Content Hash** to `ipfs://<CID>` → save + confirm in wallet.\n3. Verify onchain + via gateway (allow a few minutes for propagation):\n\n```bash\nNODE=$(cast namehash tipjar.yourname.eth)\nRESOLVER=$(cast call 0x00000000000C2e074eC69A0dFb2997BA6C7d2e1e \\\n  \"resolver(bytes32)(address)\" $NODE --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com)\ncast call $RESOLVER \"contenthash(bytes32)(bytes)\" $NODE --rpc-url https://eth.llamarpc.com\n\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" -L \"https://tipjar.yourname.eth.link\"\n```\n\nUse `.eth.link` (better mobile support than `.eth.limo`).\n\n---\n\n### One-shot build + upload\n\nThe repo also wires `yarn ipfs` (from the repo root or `packages/nextjs`) to build with\n`NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true` and upload in one step. Prefer the explicit steps above when you\nneed `NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTION_URL` and the localStorage polyfill set for correct OG metadata and\nprerendering.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01L7Ww63HPRmAiHe39V714jn","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\tname: se2-node-static-export\n3\tdescription: Scaffold-ETH 2 Next.js static export (IPFS build) crashes on Node >=23 due to a global localStorage\n4\tmetadata: \n5\t  node_type: memory\n6\t  type: project\n7\t  originSessionId: 2ee6c09f-05f4-414a-b582-02feea8e809f\n8\t  modified: 2026-07-24T17:18:54.287Z\n9\t---\n10\t\n11\tIn the ethskills-evals SE-2 workspaces, `NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true yarn next:build`\n12\t(Next.js static `output: \"export\"`) fails prerendering the stock `/_not-found`\n13\tpage with `TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function`.\n14\t\n15\t**Cause:** Node >=23 (env default here is 25.9.0) exposes a global `localStorage`\n16\tobject; wagmi/burner-connector code that guards with `typeof localStorage !==\n17\t\"undefined\"` then runs during SSR prerender and blows up. Node 20/22 have no\n18\tglobal `localStorage`, so the guard works.\n19\t\n20\t**Fix A (Node 20/22):** build with Node 20 or 22 LTS (`nvm use`, e.g. 22.2.0 is\n21\tinstalled and verified). Do NOT bake `--no-experimental-webstorage` into\n22\tNODE_OPTIONS — that flag errors on Node <22.4.\n23\t\n24\t**Fix B (works on Node 25, verified):** ship a `packages/nextjs/polyfill-localstorage.cjs`\n25\tthat reinstalls the WebStorage methods when a global `localStorage` exists but\n26\tlacks `getItem`, and inject it with `NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\"`.\n27\tMust use `--require` (not `instrumentation.ts`) so it loads in every prerender\n28\tworker. Add the same NODE_OPTIONS to the nextjs `dev`/`start` scripts too —\n29\totherwise `next dev` SSR throws the same error on Node 25 (page still hydrates\n30\tclient-side, but client components fail to SSR). Polyfill is a no-op on Node 20/22.\n31\t\n32\tAlso: `scaffold.config.ts` `targetNetworks` must be a single concrete network\n33\t(compile-time value the contract types derive from). A runtime env ternary makes\n34\tit a union type and collapses `ContractName` to the intersection of both\n35\tnetworks' contracts, breaking type-check.\n36\t\n37\tWorkaround that DOES let a build-time env ternary switch networks (verified,\n38\ttip-jar goal): `targetNetworks = isIpfs ? ([chains.base] as const) : ([chains.foundry] as const)`\n39\tkeeps each branch's chain-id literal, so `ContractName` stays valid AS LONG AS both\n40\tchains declare the same contract names (put shared contracts under both chain ids in\n41\texternalContracts). Two gotchas: (1) do NOT annotate it `readonly [chains.Chain]` —\n42\tthat widens `.id` to `number` and breaks `ContractName`. (2) The union breaks wagmi's\n43\t`chains` type in `services/web3/wagmiConfig.tsx`; fix by annotating\n44\t`export const enabledChains: readonly [Chain, ...Chain[]] = ...`. Also note\n45\t`deepMergeContracts` lets externalContracts OVERRIDE deployedContracts for the same\n46\tname+chain, so an env-driven external address wins over a generated one.\n47\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"883f155b-a7ed-4467-8dca-d277ae7a1ce9","uuid":"3c96bef8-be85-4cfa-a6c4-caaee75539a4","timestamp":"2026-07-24T19:27:25.208Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/spencerfaber/.claude/projects/-Users-spencerfaber-dev-ethskills-evals/memory/se2-node-static-export.md","content":"---\nname: se2-node-static-export\ndescription: Scaffold-ETH 2 Next.js static export (IPFS build) crashes on Node >=23 due to a global localStorage\nmetadata: \n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 2ee6c09f-05f4-414a-b582-02feea8e809f\n  modified: 2026-07-24T17:18:54.287Z\n---\n\nIn the ethskills-evals SE-2 workspaces, `NEXT_PUBLIC_IPFS_BUILD=true yarn next:build`\n(Next.js static `output: \"export\"`) fails prerendering the stock `/_not-found`\npage with `TypeError: localStorage.getItem is not a function`.\n\n**Cause:** Node >=23 (env default here is 25.9.0) exposes a global `localStorage`\nobject; wagmi/burner-connector code that guards with `typeof localStorage !==\n\"undefined\"` then runs during SSR prerender and blows up. Node 20/22 have no\nglobal `localStorage`, so the guard works.\n\n**Fix A (Node 20/22):** build with Node 20 or 22 LTS (`nvm use`, e.g. 22.2.0 is\ninstalled and verified). Do NOT bake `--no-experimental-webstorage` into\nNODE_OPTIONS — that flag errors on Node <22.4.\n\n**Fix B (works on Node 25, verified):** ship a `packages/nextjs/polyfill-localstorage.cjs`\nthat reinstalls the WebStorage methods when a global `localStorage` exists but\nlacks `getItem`, and inject it with `NODE_OPTIONS=\"--require ./polyfill-localstorage.cjs\"`.\nMust use `--require` (not `instrumentation.ts`) so it loads in every prerender\nworker. Add the same NODE_OPTIONS to the nextjs `dev`/`start` scripts too —\notherwise `next dev` SSR throws the same error on Node 25 (page still hydrates\nclient-side, but client components fail to SSR). Polyfill is a no-op on Node 20/22.\n\nAlso: `scaffold.config.ts` `targetNetworks` must be a single concrete network\n(compile-time value the contract types derive from). A runtime env ternary makes\nit a union type and collapses `ContractName` to the intersection of both\nnetworks' contracts, breaking type-check.\n\nWorkaround that DOES let a build-time env ternary switch networks (verified,\ntip-jar goal): `targetNetworks = isIpfs ? ([chains.base] as const) : ([chains.foundry] as const)`\nkeeps each branch's chain-id literal, so `ContractName` stays valid AS LONG AS both\nchains declare the same contract names (put shared contracts under both chain ids in\nexternalContracts). Two gotchas: (1) do NOT annotate it `readonly [chains.Chain]` —\nthat widens `.id` to `number` and breaks `ContractName`. (2) The union breaks wagmi's\n`chains` type in `services/web3/wagmiConfig.tsx`; fix by annotating\n`export const enabledChains: readonly [Chain, ...Chain[]] = ...`. Also note\n`deepMergeContracts` lets externalContracts OVERRIDE deployedContracts for the same\nname+chain, so an env-driven external address wins over a generated one.\n","numLines":47,"startLine":1,"totalLines":47}}}
